stories.headline: Nvidia and Japan launch national physical-AI factory with 27,500 Rubin GPUs and 140MW

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced on July 16, 2026 that it is working with Noetra Corp. to build a Vera Rubin AI factory with 13,750 Vera CPUs and 27,500 Rubin GPUs, delivering 140 megawatts of data center capacity on the Nvidia DSX platform.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA to partner with Noetra Corp. to build the NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factory with 13,750 Vera CPUs and 27,500 Rubin GPUs to deliver 140 megawatts of data center capacity based on the NVIDIA DSX platform.

key_facts.fact: The initiative is supported by Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) and provides the computing foundation for Japan's FRONTia Project, a program to develop multimodal foundation models for AI robotics and physical AI.
key_facts.excerpt: The NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factory will provide the computing foundation for Japan's FRONTia Project, which refers to the project titled, 'Development of Multimodal Foundation Models with a View to AI Robotics and Physical AI,' launched by METI.

key_facts.fact: Noetra has been allocated 387.3 billion yen ($2.4 billion) in Japanese government funds through March of next year, and dozens of companies including Sony Group, SoftBank, Toyota-backed Preferred Networks and NEC are helping set up and operate it.
key_facts.excerpt: Newly established Noetra, which has been allocated ¥387.3 billion ($2.4 billion) from government coffers through March of next year, said it will oversee the endeavor and build a roughly 140 megawatt data center. Dozens of companies including Sony Group, SoftBank, Toyota-backed Preferred Networks and NEC are helping to set up and operate Noetra.

key_facts.fact: Noetra's data center is slated to go online in June 2028, and the pretrained weights of its multimodal foundation models will be made broadly available to domestic model developers and enterprises.
key_facts.excerpt: Noetra's data center is slated to go online in June 2028. Its Rubin order, while sizable, is small compared with plans by Microsoft to eventually build data centers scaling hundreds of thousands of Nvidia's Vera Rubin systems.

key_facts.fact: Japan's AI Robotics Strategy, released in March 2026, targets capturing more than 30% of the global AI robotics market by 2040, an estimated $133 billion opportunity.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's AI Robotics Strategy, released in March, sets a goal for the country to capture more than 30% of the global AI robotics market by 2040, representing an estimated $133 billion opportunity.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang framed the deal around Japanese manufacturing: 'Japan invented modern manufacturing. Now, it is building the AI factories that will power the next industrial revolution.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Japan invented modern manufacturing. Now, it is building the AI factories that will power the next industrial revolution," said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA.

stories.headline: China's CXMT draws subscriptions for record $8.5B chip IPO as memory stocks crater worldwide

key_facts.fact: Online and offline subscriptions for ChangXin Memory Technologies' Shanghai STAR Market IPO took place on Thursday, July 16, with the company priced at 8.66 yuan ($1.28) a share to raise gross proceeds of 57.9 billion yuan ($8.5 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: The firm, based in Hefei, Anhui province, is expected to raise gross proceeds of 57.9 billion yuan (US$8.5 billion) from the sale of nearly 6.7 billion shares... Online and offline subscriptions will take place on Thursday, but CXMT has not yet announced a trading debut date.

key_facts.fact: The offering values CXMT at 579 billion yuan ($85.2 billion) and would be the largest A-share IPO ever by a Chinese chip company, surpassing SMIC's 2020 Shanghai listing that raised 53.23 billion yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: The shares represent 10 per cent of the company's enlarged capital, giving CXMT an implied valuation of 579 billion yuan (US$85.2 billion) upon listing on Shanghai's Star Market... the offering is set to surpass the 2020 Shanghai listing of Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation, which raised 53.23 billion yuan.

key_facts.fact: Memory and storage stocks fell sharply in the July 16 US session: SanDisk closed down 12.63%, Seagate 10%, Western Digital 9.15%, Intel 5.84% and Micron 5.65%.
key_facts.excerpt: US stocks of chip, memory, and storage makers fell sharply on Thursday; SNDK closed down 12.63%, STX 10%, Western Digital 9.15%, Intel 5.84%, and Micron 5.65%

key_facts.fact: Investors fear the fundraising will finance capacity expansion that worsens global DRAM oversupply; CXMT's DRAM market share reached 8% in the first quarter, making it the world's fourth-largest player, while Samsung Electronics fell 8.77% and SK Hynix 11.53% in Seoul.
key_facts.excerpt: The immediate catalyst for the market panic was China's CXMT preparing to launch an $8.55 billion IPO on the Shanghai STAR Market, with investors fearing the fundraising-driven capacity expansion will exacerbate global DRAM oversupply and price competition. CXMT's market share already climbed to 8% in the first quarter, making it the world's fourth-largest DRAM player. Meanwhile, South Korean memory giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix saw their shares drop 8.77% and 11.53%, respectively.

key_facts.fact: Micron's market capitalization fell below $1 trillion during the July 16 selloff, which followed a prior session in which Micron plunged 8% and SK Hynix ADRs tumbled 9%.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron Technology shares fell more than 4%, pushing its market capitalization below the $1 trillion mark... The selloff followed a brutal prior session where Micron plunged 8% and SK Hynix ADRs tumbled 9%.

key_facts.fact: CXMT reported first-quarter 2026 revenue of 50.8 billion yuan, up 719% year over year, with net profit of 24.762 billion yuan, up 1,688%, and forecasts first-half revenue of 110-120 billion yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: In Q1 2026, the company achieved a total revenue of 50.8 billion yuan, representing a 719% year-on-year growth, with net profit attributable to shareholders reaching 24.762 billion yuan, a 1688% year-on-year increase. The company forecasts that its total revenue for the first half of 2026 will reach between 110 billion yuan and 120 billion yuan.

key_facts.fact: Micron, SanDisk and SK Hynix have fallen roughly 30-35% from recent highs even as Micron reported record revenue and said high-bandwidth memory remains sold out well into future production.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron, Sandisk, and SK hynix have crashed 30 to 35% despite record revenues and HBM supply sold out well into future production quarters... Micron's latest earnings release showed record revenue, while management said high-bandwidth memory (HBM) remains sold out well into future production.

stories.headline: UK robot maker Humanoid raises $150M first tranche of Series A at $1.2B pre-money valuation

key_facts.fact: London-based robotics startup Humanoid raised $150 million in the first tranche of a Series A round at a $1.2 billion pre-money valuation, and is seeking another $80 million to $100 million by September.
key_facts.excerpt: Source: UK robotics startup Humanoid raised $150M in the first tranche of a Series A at a $1.2B pre-money valuation and seeks another $80M-$100M by September— Humanoid raised $150 million in the first tranche of a Series A funding round that values the London-based robotics company at $1.2 billion

key_facts.fact: Humanoid had been seeking $200 million at a valuation around $1 billion, in a deal involving Saudi Arabian energy conglomerate Aramco.
key_facts.excerpt: London-based Humanoid is seeking $200m in a deal that would value the robotics startup at around $1bn... Humanoid is working on two robots: one for industrial use cases, and one for people to have in their homes

key_facts.fact: Humanoid was founded in 2024 by Artem Sokolov, who scaled the Sokolov jewelry business into a billion-dollar manufacturing firm; the company has about 130 employees and has raised $74 million to date.
key_facts.excerpt: Humanoid was founded in 2024 by Artem Sokolov, who scaled the Sokolov jewelry business into a billion-dollar manufacturing firm. Still just 130 people, Humanoid has already signed deployment deals with Schaeffler, Bosch and Siemens and launched both bipedal and wheeled humanoid prototypes... Humanoid has raised $74 million in funding so far, but local rivals like Neura Robotics in Germany have raised over $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: The company has signed deployment deals with Schaeffler, Bosch and Siemens and has launched both bipedal and wheeled humanoid prototypes, its HMND 01 line.
key_facts.excerpt: Humanoid has already signed deployment deals with Schaeffler, Bosch and Siemens and launched both bipedal and wheeled humanoid prototypes, all without raising the billion-plus dollars of venture capital its best-known competitors enjoy.

key_facts.fact: In May 2026 Humanoid unveiled KinetIQ, a Vision-Language-Action model it says can teach humanoid robots new physical skills in two days via simulation training and real-world transfer, with mass production planned for 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: London-based robotics startup Humanoid has unveiled KinetIQ, a Vision-Language-Action model it claims can teach humanoid robots new physical skills in two calendar days through simulation-based training followed by real-world transfer, as the company seeks around $200 million in a Series A round to fund mass production planned for 2027.

stories.headline: Tata will start India's first big chip fab on 90nm, not 28nm, pushing output to mid-2028

key_facts.fact: Tata Electronics is preparing to build India's first large-scale chip fab mostly based on 90-nanometer process technology at its Dholera facility in Gujarat, far older technology than the 28nm node Tata Sons had earlier touted.
key_facts.excerpt: The tech arm of the sprawling Tata conglomerate is preparing to build the country's first large-scale chip fab or production plant mostly based on 90-nanometer process technology at its facility at Dholera in western Gujarat state, said people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified discussing private deliberations.

key_facts.fact: A Tata Electronics spokesperson said the Dholera fab will manufacture chips spanning 28nm to 110nm, and that the plan 'was always to start with 55nm and 90nm, followed by 28nm,' adding 28nm 'will be a key part of our offering.'
key_facts.excerpt: A spokesperson for Tata Electronics said the Dholera fab will manufacture chips spanning 28nm to 110nm. The plan "was always to start with 55nm and 90nm, followed by 28nm," the spokesperson said, adding that 28nm "will be a key part of our offering."

key_facts.fact: Tata had previously aimed to begin commercial production by the end of 2026, but India's technology minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told reporters on Wednesday that the Dholera plant is expected to start commercial operations in mid-2028.
key_facts.excerpt: While Tata had previously aimed to begin commercial production by the end of 2026, India's technology minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told reporters on Wednesday that the Dholera plant is expected to start commercial operations in mid-2028.

key_facts.fact: The Dholera fab is being built with a planned capital expenditure of $10.7 billion, supported by India's 2021 $10 billion aid package that offered to bear half the cost of semiconductor projects.
key_facts.excerpt: The new incentives will complement India's earlier $10 billion aid package announced in 2021, which offered to bear half the cost of setting up semiconductor projects including Tata's Dholera fab — which is being built with a planned capital expenditure of $10.7 billion and one that was initially expected to start with the 28nm chips.

key_facts.fact: The 300mm fab is being built in partnership with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC) and is designed for up to 50,000 wafers a month across 28nm to 110nm nodes; PSMC spokesperson Eric Tang said the partnership covers multiple nodes, with 28nm the most advanced.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan-based Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp (PSMC)... PSMC spokesperson Eric Tang said the partnership covers multiple technology nodes, with 28nm being the most advanced process.

key_facts.fact: Beginning with 90nm rather than 28nm places Tata initially in a less lucrative segment; 28nm remains one of the industry's most commercially important mature nodes for smartphones, communications equipment, consumer electronics and vehicles.
key_facts.excerpt: Still, 28nm is among the semiconductor industry's most commercially important mature nodes, producing chips used across smartphones, communications equipment, consumer electronics and, increasingly, vehicles. Beginning instead with 90nm production suggests Tata is initially targeting a less lucrative part of the market.
